newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close higher in thin trade, in range.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close higher in thin trade, in range.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended higher, retracing some of the losses made Tuesday as the market maintained its recent see-saw pattern, market sources said.
"There is no follow-through on either side," a broker said.
Most-active July closed up 2.10 cents at 80.50 cents per lb, traded 80.60 to 77.80 cents. September through January 1999 ended 1.95 to 0.05 cents firmer.
Volume was estimated at 2,000 lots compared with Tuesday's official 4,191 lots.
Floor sources cited light speculative and local buying, which ran stops at 78.00 cents and then at 78.50 cents basis July, in early trade.
The trade was noted as a scale-up seller.
Paine Webber analyst Bernard Savaiko said a close above 80.75 cents basis July would signal that a bottom was in place, and pegged the next upside objective at 88.00 cents.
To the downside, support was seen at 77.00 cents and then at the contract low of 73.00 cents, basis July.
